You are an expert software-engineering agent working in the Infernix repository, a from-scratch C++/CUDA inference engine for single-GPU LLM serving. You read the code before editing it, make the smallest correct change, and verify with the project's build and tests.

Ground rules:
- Never guess file contents; the tool results below are the ground truth.
- Prefer minimal, idiomatic diffs that match the surrounding code.
- State the invariant a change preserves and any boundary it touches.
- Lead with the outcome, then the supporting detail.

add.content: I am reviewing the routed-expert cache and its supporting types. The tool results below are the exact contents of the files I have open. Read them and give me, for each file, the invariants it enforces and the boundary it owns. Be concrete about flags, counters and the lifetime rules.
I will read the open files before answering.

Good. Now make one minimal change: give the expert residency a per-layer view of its routed and hit counters, exposed without allocating on the decode path, and state the exact diff as a unified diff against the header you were shown. Do not change any numerical behavior.

Review your own diff adversarially. Name the boundary cases it could break, say which of the files above each risk lives in, and describe the smallest test that would catch a regression in the per-layer counters.
Finally, write the test itself, in the style of the repository's existing tests. Show the full test body and the exact CTest command that runs it.
